environment.description: Same NestJS microservice on ECS Fargate, but origin is only accessible through CloudFront distribution d1234abcdef.cloudfront.net. The ALB security group ingress rules restrict source to the CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing). CloudFront behavior for /ws path requires a signed URL with custom policy (CloudFront key pair ID KEXAMPLE123, expiry window 30s, IP restriction to client CIDR). The CloudFront distribution has a custom origin request policy that strips and re-signs the Upgrade header only when the CloudFront signed URL signature validates. WebSocket upgrade requests that arrive at the ALB without the X-CF-Validated: sha256-hmac header (injected by CloudFront Lambda@Edge origin-request function after signature validation) are dropped by an ALB listener rule with priority 1 that checks for the header value matching a rotating HMAC derived from the request timestamp. The Lambda@Edge function also enforces that the 'token' query parameter in the WebSocket handshake matches the subject claim embedded in the CloudFront signed URL custom policy JSON. JWT_SECRET in this environment is a 256-bit random value stored in AWS Secrets Manager, rotated every 24h.

config.load_balancer: ALB with listener rule priority 1: deny if missing X-CF-Validated header with valid rotating HMAC
config.network: Private subnet, ALB SG ingress restricted to com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing prefix list

cloudfront.policy: custom policy with 30s expiry and source IP CIDR restriction
cloudfront.lambda_edge: origin-request function validates signature, injects X-CF-Validated HMAC header, enforces token-subject binding

env_vars.JWT_SECRET: fetched from Secrets Manager at boot, 256-bit random, rotated every 24h

config.origin_access: blocked - only CloudFront prefix list IPs allowed, signed URL required with IP+time+subject binding
